lead: Columbus plumbing deals with cold winters, hard water and a mix of old brick homes and new suburbs. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Columbus.
risk: frozen pipes, hard water scale and aging pipes in older neighborhoods
risk_short: frozen pipes, hard water and old pipes
why: German Village, Victorian Village and Clintonville have homes from the late 1800s to the 1930s, with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and clay sewer laterals. Many have basements with old floor drains.
Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls. Newer suburbs add water heater, softener and fixture calls.
utility: City of Columbus Division of Water
water: Columbus draws from the Scioto River and Big Walnut Creek reservoirs and from wells. The water is hard, and the city softens it at the plant, but scale still builds up.
tips: Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in German Village, the Short North, Clintonville, Victorian Village, Hilltop, Linden and every other Columbus neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Columbus Department of Building and Zoning Services. Ohio licenses commercial plumbing contractors. The city sets the rules for home plumbing work.

faq.a: Yes. Columbus water is hard before treatment, and the city softens it at the plant. Some scale still forms over time, so flushing water heaters yearly is a good habit.
